title: Quantization experiment summary (Q4) — profiles, perf/quality results, and telemetry tagging
content:
Owner: Aditya
Last pass: 2026-01-05
Audience: Serving Runtime, Optimize, Telemetry/Analytics, Finance (for unit-econ attribution context)

Why this doc exists
- Q4 quantization work touched multiple teams (runtime kernel selection, model catalog metadata, token metering tags).
- This is a single place to capture what we tested, what moved perf/$, what regressed quality, and how to tag runs so Unit Economics can attribute $/1M output tokens by quantization_profile.

Scope / what’s included (Q4)
- Models tested (representative):
  - rw-llama-3.1-8b-instruct (internal bundle)
  - rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct (internal bundle)
  - rw-qwen2.5-32b-instruct (internal bundle)
  - Embeddings/rerank models were NOT included in this pass.
- Hardware tested:
  - NVIDIA H100 SXM (80GB) — primary
  - NVIDIA A100 (80GB) — secondary
  - NVIDIA L40S (48GB) — opportunistic sanity checks only
- Serving patterns:
  - Chat completion style workloads
  - Mix of short prompts and long-context prompts (8k–32k), with and without streaming

Quick glossary (as used here)
- Profile: a named quantization configuration that should be stable, low-cardinality, and attributable in telemetry.
- TTFT: time to first token (p50/p95)
- Decode TPS: steady-state tokens/sec during decode (p50/p95)
- Prefill: compute dominated by prompt/context ingestion
- Quality: delta on eval sets + targeted regressions (tool/function calling JSON validity, refusal rate, and internal “support-style” prompts)

Experiment setup (what we tried)
We tested a small set of “production candidate” profiles with an emphasis on:
- measurable $/token impact (via throughput improvements and/or lower required GPU class)
- stability for long contexts (KV cache + attention path issues are where most surprises happen)
- minimal quality regression and predictable failure modes

Profiles tested (naming is what we want in telemetry; see tagging section)
1) fp16_baseline
- Reference profile for each model/hardware.
- Used to anchor perf and quality deltas.

2) bf16_baseline
- Mostly equivalent to fp16 on our kernels; included for completeness and to compare vendor stacks.

3) fp8_e4m3_h100
- H100-specific profile using FP8 (E4M3) in supported matmuls.
- Not intended for A100/L40S.

4) int8_weight_only_awq
- Weight-only INT8 (AWQ-style).
- Candidate for broad deployment; tends to trade small quality shifts for better decode throughput.

5) int4_weight_only_gptq
- Weight-only INT4 (GPTQ-style).
- High variance: can be great on decode throughput, but more fragile on long-context + certain model families.

6) int8_smoothquant_actaware
- “Act-aware”/SmoothQuant-like approach where applicable.
- Harder to operationalize due to calibration artifacts and model-specific requirements.

Note: We intentionally did NOT add a pile of variants (different group sizes, per-channel settings, etc.) because telemetry + dashboard requires low cardinality. Variants belong in offline experiment IDs, not the runtime quantization_profile dimension.

Results summary (high-level takeaways)
1) H100: fp8_e4m3_h100 is the biggest reliable win (when supported)
- For 70B class models on H100, FP8 consistently improved decode throughput at similar or slightly improved p95 latency under load.
- TTFT did not always improve (prefill remains a bottleneck for long prompts); decode and capacity were where we saw the win.
- Quality: no statistically meaningful degradation on our general eval set; a couple small shifts on structured output validity were observed (details below).

2) int8_weight_only_awq is the best “portable” profile across H100 + A100
- Consistent decode TPS improvement on both H100 and A100.
- Long-context behavior generally stable.
- Quality: small but noticeable degradation on certain instruction-following prompts for one model family (8B instruct) — likely recoverable with profile tuning or model-specific exceptions.

3) int4_weight_only_gptq is not ready as a default production profile
- Great on raw throughput in some short-context decode-heavy slices.
- Several unacceptable tails:
  - higher p95 TTFT under multi-tenant load
  - occasional instability for long contexts (KV cache interactions; needs more runtime hardening)
  - quality regressions on “precision-sensitive” tasks (mathy / extraction)

4) SmoothQuant-ish profiles are promising but operationally expensive
- Requires careful calibration artifacts and model-specific packaging.
- Without a clean “model onboarding + artifact management” story, it’s hard to scale this across our catalog.

Representative numbers (directional; see note)
Important: These are directional and workload-dependent. Do not quote publicly. The goal is to decide which profiles we can operationalize and how to tag them so Unit Economics can measure impact.

Workload A (chat, ~1–2k prompt, ~300 output, moderate concurrency)
- 70B on H100:
  - fp16_baseline: baseline
  - fp8_e4m3_h100: ~+20–35% decode TPS; p95 latency improved ~10–20% under load
  - int8_weight_only_awq: ~+10–20% decode TPS; smaller latency win
- 32B on A100:
  - fp16_baseline: baseline
  - int8_weight_only_awq: ~+10–18% decode TPS; p95 latency slightly better or flat
  - int4_weight_only_gptq: highly variable; can be +20% TPS but with worse p95 tails

Workload B (long context, 16k–32k prompt, ~200 output)
- Biggest driver is prefill cost; quantization helps but less dramatically.
- fp8_e4m3_h100 helped overall wall time mostly through improved throughput under concurrency; TTFT improvements were not guaranteed.

Quality evaluation summary
Eval sets used (Q4)
- Internal “prod-ish” prompt set (support agent, coding assistant, extraction)
- JSON / structured-output validity harness (tool calling + schema-constrained outputs)
- Long-context consistency probes (needle-in-haystack-ish, multi-document QA)
- Light-weight external sanity (MT-Bench style prompts) — used for spot-checking only, not for go/no-go

Notable observations
- fp8_e4m3_h100:
  - Overall: best quality/perf trade-off.
  - Watch-outs: Slight increase in malformed JSON rate in one configuration when temperature > 0.7 (could be unrelated; needs controlled rerun).

- int8_weight_only_awq:
  - Generally acceptable.
  - One model (8B instruct) showed small regression in “follow constraints exactly” prompts (more extra text outside JSON). If this repeats, we may need:
    - a model-specific default profile (keep fp16 for that model)
    - or enforce stricter decoding / structured-output constraints in the gateway for that route

- int4_weight_only_gptq:
  - Regression hot spots:
    - extraction accuracy
    - math reasoning
    - long-context multi-hop
  - Recommendation: keep as an experimental opt-in only (not a catalog default) until runtime and model packaging mature.

Operational recommendations (what we should do next)
Catalog defaults (proposed)
- H100 deployments:
  - Default to fp8_e4m3_h100 where supported and validated per model.
  - Fall back to int8_weight_only_awq (or fp16) for unsupported models.
- A100 deployments:
  - Default to int8_weight_only_awq for models that pass the structured-output validity thresholds.
  - Keep fp16_baseline for the small set of models/prompts that show regressions.

Quality guardrails (proposed gates)
- Structured output / tool calls:
  - malformed JSON rate must not exceed baseline by >0.3 pp (absolute) on the harness
- Long-context:
  - no more than 1% absolute drop on the long-context probes (pass/fail style)
- “Don’t surprise the customer” gate:
  - any regression that changes refusal/unsafe behavior requires review (even if perf wins are large)

Telemetry + Unit Economics attribution: how to tag runs (IMPORTANT)
Goal: Unit Economics dashboard needs a stable dimension quantization_profile to attribute blended $/1M output tokens, and to correlate cost shifts with quantization rollouts.

What needs to be tagged
- Every request (and therefore every metering event) should carry:
  - model_id (canonical)
  - model_version (or model_build)
  - quantization_profile (string from allowed set)
  - hardware_class (optional in metering, but captured in infra cost allocation / runtime)
  - region + customer_tier (handled elsewhere, but mentioned because slicing without quant_profile is misleading)

Allowed values (proposed stable set)
We need low cardinality + human-readable + forward compatible. Proposed allowed values:
- fp16_baseline
- bf16_baseline
- fp8_e4m3_h100
- int8_weight_only_awq
- int4_weight_only_gptq
- int8_smoothquant_actaware
- unknown (fallback only; should alert if >0.1% of tokens)

Rules
- Do NOT emit raw experiment IDs, git SHAs, or calibration artifact names in quantization_profile.
- Do NOT include model name in quantization_profile (it’s already a separate dimension).
- Do NOT include hardware in the profile except for explicitly hardware-bound ones (fp8_e4m3_h100 is the one exception we’re making).
- If a profile changes materially (e.g., AWQ group size change that affects perf/quality), bump the profile name (e.g., int8_weight_only_awq_v2) ONLY if Finance/Telemetry agree the dashboard needs to distinguish it. Prefer keeping the profile stable and tracking variants via offline experiment metadata.

Where to set the tag
- Runtime should expose the active quantization profile as part of request metadata.
- Gateway should forward this into token metering events.
- Telemetry pipeline should enforce allowed values and coerce unknowns.

Implementation notes / pointers
- See GitHub:redwood/pr-19370-add-quantization-profile-to-request-metadata (adds request metadata + allowed-value constraints).
- See Linear:ENG-8425 for pipeline + dimension plumbing.
- Cardinality guidance: Confluence token-metering-dimensions-and-cardinality

Suggested validation queries (for telemetry sanity)
- Coverage: For a given day, percentage of output tokens with quantization_profile != 'unknown'
- Distribution: Top profiles by output tokens; watch for new unexpected values
- Parity check: Compare streaming vs non-streaming paths (quant_profile should be present for both)

Known gaps / TODOs
- Need rerun: fp8_e4m3_h100 JSON validity issue at higher temperature; confirm if real.
- Need clearer mapping in model catalog: which models are “fp8 eligible” vs fallback.
- Need a single place to define per-model default quant profile + rollout policy (likely belongs in model metadata / routing policy docs owned by Quentin).
- Need to ensure “quantization_profile” is included in any canary / regression tests for output token metering so we don’t lose attribution during refactors.

Appendix: experiment bookkeeping (what we stored)
- Offline experiment IDs live in the Applied ML experiments tracker (not linked here because it contains ad-hoc notes and temp artifact paths).
- For any experiment that looks production-worthy, we should create a short follow-up note with:
  - model_id + version
  - candidate quantization_profile (from allowed set)
  - hardware class
  - pass/fail on guardrails
  - recommended rollout sequence (internal -> hosted self-serve -> dedicated -> private)

Questions / asks
- Telemetry (Nadia): confirm whether quantization_profile is attached at the right event layer for both streaming and non-streaming metering.
- Model metadata (Quentin): propose where default profile selection lives (catalog vs runtime config) and how it’s versioned.
- Optimize/Product (Marissa/Aditya): confirm how the Unit Economics dashboard should present quant_profile (filter + drilldown) without confusing Finance (i.e., blended vs marginal cost).
